predecessors.name: Satavahana dynasty
predecessors.text: the Nasik region, the "northern parts of the kingdom, around Nashik region" that the Abhiras captured from the Satavahanas

predecessors.name: Western Satraps
predecessors.text: Lata, Aparanta and Khandesh, ruled by Kshatrapa governors before the Abhiras

successors.name: Traikutaka dynasty
successors.text: Aparanta (northern Konkan), northern Maharashtra and southern Gujarat

successors.name: Vakataka dynasty
successors.text: the northern Abhira domains, lost to "the rising Vakatakas (north)"

ledger.x: c. 203: the Abhiras capture the Nasik region from the Satavahanas. Infobox: "Period 203 to roughly 270 or 370 CE" (the basis of 203 is not given); Satavahana page: "During Yajna's last years, the Abhiras captured the northern parts of the kingdom, around Nashik region", with Yajna ruling 170-199 (Sen) and his reign…

c. 249: Ishwarsena starts the Abhira era and rules Khandesh and Ashmaka. "Ishwarsena started an era to commemorate his ascension in 284 or 249 AD"; his controlled areas "included Lata, Aparanta, Khandesh, and Ashmaka (Andhra), with Nasik as the core"; "about A.D. 250 the Satavahanas were replaced by the Abhiras in…

c. 249: Ishwarsena rules Aparanta and Lata. The Ishwarsena page lists both among his areas but gives no date or previous owner; the Kshatrapa counterpart is the Abhira page's ("Abhira chiefs served as generals" of the Western Satraps; Malwa "taken from the Kshatrapas"). Cliopatria keeps the Western Satraps over Lata…

c. 370: the last Abhira chieftains disappear. "many petty Abhira chieftains and kings continued to rule until the fourth century, roughly till 370 AD"; the infobox says "roughly 270 or 370" and puts the Traikutaka takeover at 315 or 370; the Traikutaka page starts the successor c. 388.

wars.name: Abhira capture of the northern Satavahana lands
wars.outcome: The Abhiras take the Nasik region from the last Satavahanas.

certainty.note: No border is given for any year; the Abhira domains are named by region only (Nasik core, Aparanta, Lata, Khandesh, Ashmaka) and are undated beyond the era of Ishwarsena.
